title: Dropping a new sidebar favorite ignores the drop position
reasoning: The outline view passes the proposed child index into acceptExternalDrop, but the helper never uses targetIndex and always appends new custom favorites. A user dropping a folder between existing favorites gets it at the end instead, which contradicts the drop indicator and makes ordering unreliable.
reproduction: Drag a folder into the Favorites section above an existing custom favorite. The drop is accepted, but the new SidebarItem is appended to customFavs instead of inserted at the proposed child index.
recommendation: Translate targetIndex into the custom-favorites index after accounting for built-in favorites, clamp it, and insert new items there while preserving multi-item order.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No included tests exercise SidebarViewController drag/drop or SidebarItem custom-favorite ordering.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a sidebar drop-order test with existing custom favorites and a proposed child index before the last item, then assert saveCustomFavorites receives the new item at that position.

history.reasoning: The original evidence path still exists. At Grove/Controllers/SidebarViewController.swift:190-194, acceptDrop still forwards the proposed child index to acceptExternalDrop. The helper at Grove/Controllers/SidebarViewController.swift:233-277 no longer ignores targetIndex: it computes a custom-favorites insertion index after subtracting built-in favorites, clamps it, inserts each dropped item at that index, and increments for multi-item drops. git diff confirms the old customFavs.append(newItem) in acceptExternalDrop was replaced with customFavs.insert(newItem, at: customTargetIndex). The remaining customFavs.append(newItem) is in addFavorite, not the drag/drop path. Xcode test/list validation could not run in this read-only sandbox because xcodebuild could not create xcrun/DerivedData/result-bundle files, but current code evidence shows the reported drag/drop ordering bug is fixed.
